subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Does a crafted `__proto__` or `constructor` value reach an unsafe merge or assignment sink in any authenticated Gateway request handler on current main?
rationale: The reported parsing architecture is inaccurate and JSON parsing alone is not an exploit, but only a security-owner audit of downstream method handlers can safely settle whether a real prototype-mutation boundary exists.

options.title: Run a targeted sink audit
options.body: Privately test representative merge, patch, config, and persistence handlers with crafted authenticated frames, fixing only a demonstrated unsafe sink.

options.title: Adopt global key rejection
options.body: Treat restricted prototype keys as invalid across all Gateway payloads and accept the resulting compatibility change as defense in depth.

options.title: Close after source audit
options.body: Close as unsupported if security review confirms every relevant handler validates or safely copies caller-controlled objects without a mutation sink.

recommendation.title: Run a targeted sink audit
recommendation.body: Privately test representative merge, patch, config, and persistence handlers with crafted authenticated frames, fixing only a demonstrated unsafe sink.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest adjacent history signal is recent work on Gateway authentication and trusted-input security boundaries.
